The pilot

One squad. One season. No club-wide commitment.

Roster loaded, season phase set, your crest on every screen a Dogs family sees. Nothing to install — it runs in a phone browser and can be added to a home screen.

And a note home to guardians saying exactly what is and is not collected. Consent is gathered before any athlete appears on a board.

Athletes record their own work and we watch for the dull problems — a phone propped where it cannot see, a drill whose target needs adjusting for this age group.

Assignments, film and the pre-practice list. By now the workload baseline is real enough that the load flags mean something.

A written read on what the squad actually did, and the full data export. If you walk away, you take it with you.

What we would need from you

One squad, a roster in whatever format you already keep it, fifteen minutes of a coaches' meeting, one member of staff as the point of contact, and honest feedback — including the parts you dislike.

Before you say yes

What this does not do.

It does not coach. It counts reps and shows patterns. What to do about a pattern is your job and it is not being automated.

It does not watch a game. Nothing here scores a save, a dodge, or a decision under pressure. It measures solo, repeatable work.

It is not medical. The load flags are a prompt for a conversation, not a diagnosis, and the app says so wherever it raises one.

And one thing that is simply true today: the calibration behind the rep counters was built on older athletes. A season with a 2031 age group is what makes it right for thirteen-year-olds — which is part of why we are asking you.

Your answer

Worth a season?
